_readme: PAYLOAD FIXTURE for `src/sources/push-capture.ts`.
One capture as that adapter's `fetch` returns it: the versioned
envelope `src/lib/capture-contract.ts` describes, whole, with a
body carrying two records under `items`. `parse` and
`toCanonical` are driven over it with no network, which is what
keeps the cases beside that module in the fully isolated default
suite. For a push source that seam is the ordinary path rather
than a stand-in: the stored payload IS the source.
An envelope, not the payload itself: everything the adapter is
handed sits under `payload`, and this key does not. A header
written into the payload would reach `parse` as though a client
had posted it.
AUTHORED, not captured. Every host is under `.invalid`, which is
reserved and resolves nowhere, and the two records are about
nothing and nobody. A fixture is committed, and a real capture
pasted in whole is the easiest way to commit somebody else's
data by accident.
The two records differ on purpose. The first carries markup the
`body` field reads through a selector; the second carries no
`markup` member at all, so that field reads nothing and the
document is kept with an empty body and a warning. `sourceId`
here is the row the client CLAIMS to be posting against, and the
cases construct the adapter for a different one so that the
claim and the column can be told apart.
